model_annotation: The image presents two grouped bar charts, comparing the percentage of Aluminium, Kupfer (Copper), and Nickel in Deutschland (Germany) and the EU over three years: 2021, 2022, and 2023, representing data in percentage. The horizontal axis lists the metals: Aluminium, Kupfer, and Nickel, while the vertical axis represents the percentage, ranging from 0% to 30% in increments of 5%. Each metal is represented by a group of three bars, colored blue (2021), purple (2022), and grey (2023), allowing for a clear visual comparison of the data across the years and between the two regions. In Deutschland, Aluminium percentages decreased from 3.6% in 2021 to 2.7% in 2022 and further to 1.0% in 2023, while Kupfer increased from 8.3% in 2021 to 11.3% in 2022, then dropped to 2.2% in 2023, and Nickel remained relatively stable, with 25.1% in 2021, 24.7% in 2022, and 11.4% in 2023. Similarly, in the EU, Aluminium percentages decreased from 3.2% in 2021 to 2.8% in 2022 and further to 1.7% in 2023, Kupfer showed a slight increase from 4.4% in 2021 to 5.1% in 2022, then decreased to 1.3% in 2023, and Nickel percentages decreased from 24.3% in 2021 to 23.3% in 2022 and further to 14.6% in 2023. Overall, the charts provide a clear visual representation of the trends and changes in the percentages of these metals in Deutschland and the EU over the three-year period, with Nickel consistently having the highest percentage among the three metals in both regions.
